lipodystrophy.definition: A change in where the body stores fat. In some people on HIV treatment, fat is lost in some places and builds up in the belly.

visceral-fat.definition: Fat stored deep inside the belly, around the organs. It is different from the fat just under the skin.

lipolysis.definition: The breakdown of stored fat into fatty acids that the body can use for energy.

acromegaly.definition: A disease caused by too much growth hormone in adults. Hands, feet and the face slowly grow larger, and diabetes and heart problems become more common.

carpal-tunnel-syndrome.definition: Numbness, tingling or pain in the hand and fingers when a nerve at the wrist is squeezed, for example by swollen tissue.

arthralgia.definition: Pain in one or more joints, without visible damage to the joint.

myalgia.definition: Pain or aching in the muscles.

paraesthesia.definition: Tingling, pricking or numbness of the skin, like pins and needles, without an obvious cause.

liver-fibrosis.definition: Scar tissue that builds up in the liver after long-lasting damage, for example from too much fat. Severe scarring is called cirrhosis.

standard-deviation-score.definition: A way to say how far a lab value is from the average for people of the same age and sex. A score above 2 is unusually high; above 3 is very high.

biological-product.definition: In US law, a medicine such as a protein, vaccine or blood product. Any chain of more than 40 amino acids counts as a protein, so some large peptides are regulated as biological products.

hypersensitivity-reaction.definition: An allergic-type reaction of the immune system to a medicine. It ranges from a rash or hives to, rarely, swelling of the throat and trouble breathing.

neutralising-antibodies.definition: Antibodies that stop a medicine from working, not only stick to it.

hydrocephaly.definition: A build-up of fluid inside the spaces of the brain. In unborn animals or babies it can harm how the brain develops.

hiv.definition: A virus that weakens the immune system. HIV medicines keep it under control, so people with HIV can live long lives.

antiretroviral-therapy.definition: A combination of medicines that keeps HIV under control. Some older HIV medicines changed where the body stores fat.

ct-scan.definition: A scan that uses X-rays and a computer to make pictures of slices through the body. It can measure how much fat lies around the organs.

biopsy.definition: Taking a tiny piece of tissue, for example with a needle from the liver, to look at it under a microscope.

cytochrome-p450.definition: A family of enzymes, mostly in the liver, that break down many medicines. Anything that changes them can make other medicines stronger or weaker.

aliases: Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use
chmp.definition: The European Medicines Agency's expert committee that assesses applications for human medicines and advises whether the EU should authorise them.
